# Topic Modeling 

### Process into corpus object

```{r}
textdata <- pol_influ %>% 
  mutate(year = str_sub(published_date, 1, 4)) %>% # creates the year column
  select(filename, sentence, year) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(doc_id = filename, text = sentence)
```

### Remove stopwords, clean corpus

```{r}
# 1. Define standard stopwords
english_stopwords <- stopwords("en")

# 2. Build corpus
corpus <- Corpus(DataframeSource(textdata))

# 3. Clean in correct sequence
processedCorpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removePunctuation, preserve_intra_word_dashes = TRUE)
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeNumbers)

# Remove stopwords BEFORE stemming
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeWords, english_stopwords)

# Stem documents after removing stopwords
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stemDocument, language = "en")
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stripWhitespace)
```

```{r tm3a}
#DTM: rows correspond to the documents in the corpus. Columns correspond to the terms in the documents. Cells correspond to the weights of the terms. (Girder)
# compute document term matrix with terms >= minimumFrequency
minimumFrequency <- 5
DTM <- DocumentTermMatrix(processedCorpus, control = list(bounds = list(global = c(minimumFrequency, Inf))))
# have a look at the number of documents and terms in the matrix
dim(DTM)
# due to vocabulary pruning, we have empty rows in our DTM
# LDA does not like this. So we remove those docs from the
# DTM and the metadata
sel_idx <- slam::row_sums(DTM) > 0
DTM <- DTM[sel_idx, ]
textdata <- textdata[sel_idx, ]

# 5 term minimum [1] 117387 14223
# 5 term minimum[1] [1] 99631 14223

```

## Topic proportions over time {.unnumbered}

We examine topics in the data over time by aggregating mean topic proportions per year. These aggregated topic proportions can then be visualized, e.g. as a bar plot.

Articles per year

```{r}
#| echo: false
#install.packages("formattable")
articles_years <- textdata %>% 
  distinct(doc_id, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  count(year) %>% 
  mutate(pct_total= (n/sum(n))) %>% 
  mutate(pct_total= formattable::percent(pct_total)) %>% 
  # mutate(pct_total = round(pct_total, 1)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(year))

#library(kableExtra)
articles_years %>%
  kbl(caption = "Political Social Media Influencer Articles by Year", font_size = 30) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T, border_right = T) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "5em") %>% 
  column_spec(3, width = "5em", background = "yellow")



#Fact check total number of unique articles
#sum(articles_years$n)
```

```{r tm12}
# number of topics
# K <- 20
K <- 6
# set random number generator seed
set.seed(9161)
#Latent Dirichlet Allocation, LDA
topicModel2 <- LDA(DTM, K, method="Gibbs", control=list(iter = 500, verbose = 25, alpha = 0.2))
tmResult <- posterior(topicModel2)
theta <- tmResult$topics
beta <- tmResult$terms
topicNames <- apply(terms(topicModel2, 10), 2, paste, collapse = " ")  # reset topicnames
```

### Mean topic proportions per year

```{r}

# Step 1: Check dimensions
n_theta <- nrow(theta)
n_textdata <- length(textdata$year)

cat("Number of rows in theta: ", n_theta, "\n")
cat("Number of documents in textdata: ", n_textdata, "\n")

# Number of rows in theta: 99631
# Number of documents in textdata: 99631

# Ensure the lengths match
if (n_theta != n_textdata) {
  stop("The number of rows in 'theta' still does not match textdata.")
}

# Removed the ID-matching steps from the lesson code because theta and textdata already have matching row counts.

# Step 2: Combine data
topic_data <- data.frame(theta, year = textdata$year)

# Step 3: Aggregate data
topic_proportion_per_year <- aggregate(. ~ year, data = topic_data, FUN = mean)

# Set topic names to aggregated columns
colnames(topic_proportion_per_year)[2:(K+1)] <- topicNames

# Reshape data frame
vizDataFrame <- melt(topic_proportion_per_year, id.vars = "year")

```

#Examine topic names

```{r}
#enframe(): Converts a named list into a dataframe.
topics <- enframe(topicNames, name = "number", value = "text") %>% 
  unnest(cols = c(text)) 
  
topics
```

### Review the topics and determine a 1-2 word label after reading the source documents.

```{r}

#Topics 

theta2 <- as.data.frame(theta)

topic1 <- theta2 %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "doc_id") |> # put document IDs into a column
  mutate(doc_id = str_remove(doc_id, "^X\\."),  # remove leading "X."
         line = str_extract(doc_id, "(?<=\\.txt)\\.\\d+")) |> # Extract number after .txt
  mutate(doc_id = str_remove(doc_id, "\\.\\d+$")) |>
  rename(topic1 = '1') |> 
  top_n(20, topic1) |> 
  arrange(desc(topic1)) |>  
  select(doc_id, line, topic1)
```

```{r}

# add categories

vizDataFrame <- vizDataFrame %>% 
  mutate(category = case_when(
    str_detect(variable, "trump said presid state hous feder administr law elect govern") ~ "Trump_Administration",
    str_detect(variable, "think know peopl like end video just want get clip") ~ "Political_Broadcast",
    str_detect(variable, "said “ polit ’s — peopl like trump one word") ~ "Political_Culture",
    str_detect(variable, "new time york media post social polit campaign influenc right") ~ "Digital_politics",
    str_detect(variable, "news fox thank right now bodi presid well iran yes") ~ "Political_News",
    str_detect(variable, "democrat republican trump elect parti voter senat presid state campaign") ~ "Elections_Campaigns"
  ))

```

# Fact Check and Validate Topics

Topic 1: Trump Administration "trump said presid state hous feder administr law elect govern" Topic 2: Political Broadcast "think know peopl like end video just want get clip" Topic 3: Political Culture "said “ polit ’s — peopl like trump one word" Topic 4: Digital_politics "new time york media post social polit campaign influenc right" Topic 5: Political News "news fox thank right now bodi presid well iran yes" Topic 6: Elections and Campaigns "democrat republican trump elect parti voter senat presid state campaign"

### for trump_administration

```{r}

theta2 <- as.data.frame(theta)

trump_administration <- theta2 %>% 
  # renaming for a general topic
  rename(trump_administration = '1') %>% 
  top_n(20, trump_administration) %>%
  arrange(desc(trump_administration)) %>% 
  select(trump_administration)

# Apply rownames_to_column
trump_administration <- tibble::rownames_to_column(
  trump_administration, "story_id"
)

# Remove leading "X." if present
trump_administration$story_id <- str_remove(
  trump_administration$story_id, "^X\\."
) # Used AI to accommodate the code for my story IDs.

# Remove trailing segment number
trump_administration$story_id <- str_remove(
  trump_administration$story_id, "\\.\\d+$"
)

head(trump_administration$story_id, 20)

# Checks out

```

## Set up for hosting

- Create a new folder in your repository called "docs" (if one isn't there already)
- Rename this document as "index.qmd"
- Move "index.qmd" into the "docs" folder

## Render this document as an html page

- Make sure this document is named "index.qmd" and is in the "docs" folder
- Click Render button. It will create an html version of this page, called "index.html"
- Use GitHub Desktop to push your files to your your github repository on the web.
- Access the URL from your Github repository.

## Host html on GitHub

- Go to your github repository on the web, such as https://github.com/djnf-data-2026/casey-mann
- Click on Settings on the top right.
- Scroll down to the Pages section of Settings.
- Change the Branch to /docs and click save.

#### To see your file hosted:

- Back to your GitHub repo on the web: such as https://github.com/djnf-data-2026/casey-mann
- Click on Settings, then Pages
- Under GitHub Pages, you should see "Your site is live at https://djnf-data-2026.github.io/casey-mann/"
- Click that URL
- If it works, email it to robwells\@umd.edu
